inputs.title: The Thing
inputs.logline: When Bo’s big tail betrays how hard it is to meet new friends, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very thing he wants to hide may be the first thing everyone loves.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

beats.adultRead: The comedy is the impossibility of controlling every tell; Keen’s cover is doomed because he is still a kid in a too-big plan.
beats.emotionalIntent: Build the laugh through anticipation, release it with the sneeze, then button it with Fuzzby’s sleepy authority.

beats.need: She needs to trust the quiet signal and make room for someone else’s fear without taking over.
beats.kidRead: A magic bowl shows a squirrel who keeps packing but does not go anywhere.
beats.adultRead: The repetition is instantly recognizable as a child trying to make a hard transition feel controllable.
beats.emotionalIntent: Quiet wonder with a small ache under it; the vision should feel intimate, not flashy.

beats.storyBeat: Inside the hollow tree, Bo answers his offscreen Mum but bargains with time and his conker, delaying the Learning Circle by making “a minute” stretch absurdly. The safe room is cosy, but it is also a trap of postponement.
beats.want: Bo wants to put off leaving while sounding like he still intends to go.
beats.need: He needs to be witnessed in the stuck place instead of left alone with the loop.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps finding reasons not to go yet, and his conker is like his little helper.
beats.adultRead: The offscreen parent call captures the morning-transition ache: encouragement from another room cannot cross the threshold for him.
beats.emotionalIntent: Tender comic avoidance; keep it small, domestic and recognisable.

vision.premise: Bo is due at the Learning Circle for the first time, but every step toward the door makes his tail poof with worry. Keen’s playful curiosity and Aida’s quiet truth help him move toward the group one step at a time, until the tail he feared becomes his way in.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo go to the Learning Circle without having to hide the part of himself that gives him away?
vision.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is gently witnessed and welcomed.
vision.externalJourney: Keen fails to steal honey, is redirected by Aida, visits Bo’s hollow tree, walks him through the woods, helps him arrive at the Learning Circle, and returns home to find Fuzzby attempting his own honey heist.
vision.internalJourney: Bo moves from delaying and controlling every detail to taking a visible step forward with his worry still present, then letting his tail become play instead of proof that something is wrong with him.
vision.relationshipChanges: Bo and Keen shift from strangers at a doorway to easy friends; Bo and Aida move from cautious distance to shared truth; Bo and the Learning Circle group move from imagined judgement to delighted acceptance. Fuzzby and Zenny provide the comic echo: being ridiculous and still belonging.
vision.emotionalCurve: Playful mischief opens the episode, then narrows into Bo’s held-at-the-door worry. The woods give relief through play, dip again at the log, soften through Aida’s honesty, glow into the walk forward, burst into group joy, and settle in a warm, lightly comic garden coda.
vision.comedyCurve: The comedy starts with stealth, snore bubbles, pollen and sneezes; turns into tail-poof escalation and Keen’s useless-tail demonstration; blooms into group delight at the Learning Circle; and ends with Fuzzby’s flower-disguise failure and Zenny’s tiny crack of amusement.
vision.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s “never ever” return in the final garden heist. Bo’s conker and repeated packing plant his need for control. The tail’s first unwanted poof pays off as a chosen game in the woods and then as the Learning Circle’s delight. Aida’s vision of Bo unable to move pays off in Bo walking forward under pink and blue light. “Every single time” moves from Aida’s truth to Bo’s own action phrase.
vision.visualMotifs: Closed/open thresholds, paws holding objects too tightly, Bo’s tail expanding beyond his control, the forest path as a visible line between home and belonging, and the honeycomb as comic temptation that remains untouched.
vision.sonicMotifs: Crunching steps, snore-bubble pops, sneeze blasts, the shave-and-a-haircut knock, tail POOFs, Aida’s bowl tone, rose and aquamarine glow tones, group cheers, and Zenny’s bookend Ommmm.
vision.climax: Aida and Keen each offer their crystal truth, pink and blue light join on the forest path, and Bo takes one step, then another, toward the Learning Circle.
vision.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail poofs in front of everyone and is met with wonder, cheering and play; later, he draws with Keen while Aida watches his settled belonging from the edge of the clearing.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, giggly relief: the child feels the fun of the fluffy tail, while the adult feels the ache of a child being welcomed without needing to edit himself.

northStar.surfaceStory: Keen tries to sneak up on Fuzzby’s honeycomb while Fuzzby sleeps, but every crunchy step, snore bubble, pollen puff and warning makes the honey feel farther away.
northStar.universalTruth: Sometimes a child thinks wanting something very badly makes them ready to take it, but their own body and the world reveal they are not as invisible or in control as they imagine.
northStar.childClearWant: Keen wants the honey without waking Fuzzby.
northStar.emotionalNeed: Keen needs to feel the difference between being excited and being ready; he must discover that boldness is not the same as permission or skill.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If I move carefully enough and keep trying, I can get what I want without anyone noticing.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Keen’s hunger pushes him toward the honey; Fuzzby’s sleepy presence turns that want into a comic test of respect. Fuzzby is not an enemy — his sleep, ownership and half-awake warning are the boundary Keen keeps bumping into. Zenny’s calm arrival becomes the quiet counterweight to Keen’s over-busy sneaking.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: A child sneaking a treat before breakfast is often betrayed not by badness, but by their own little body: loud feet, itchy nose, guilty freezes, and the adult-sized hope that no one saw.
northStar.sceneTurn: The stealth game stops being a private adventure when the pollen forces Keen into a sneeze and Fuzzby briefly wakes; the honey changes from ‘almost mine’ to ‘definitely not today.’
audienceJourney: Giggle at Keen’s exaggerated tiptoe confidence.
Lean in with tiny suspense as each crunch and snore bubble threatens to wake Fuzzby.
Laugh at the sneeze collapsing the whole mission.
Enjoy Fuzzby’s possessive, sleepy overstatement without reading him as mean.
Settle on the comic promise that the honeycomb is still there, untouched, waiting to matter later.
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: Light, unfinished comic frustration: Keen has lost this round, the honey remains tempting, and the audience carries the promise that this forbidden prize will return.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any explanation of Keen’s plan, fear, guilt, or disappointment. His high-knee tiptoe, lip lick, frozen paws, sneeze recovery, and walk-away carry all of it. Do not verbalise Zenny’s judgement; her calm ‘Ommmm…’ and stillness are enough.
northStar.environmentPressure: The Buzzing Nook actively betrays stealth: crunchy ground announces every step, dew and pollen keep the air alive, wildflowers shed the exact irritant Keen cannot resist, and Fuzzby’s snore bubbles create a ticking physical trap around the honeycomb.

transformation.entryBelief: I can borrow enough boldness to sneak past Fuzzby and get the honey if I just keep going.
transformation.entryFeeling: Excited, greedy, and self-consciously brave — thrilled by the prize and nervous about being caught.
transformation.pressureBehaviour: He over-performs stealth: knees too high, body too tense, freezing at every crunch and bubble pop, then inching closer anyway because the honey keeps pulling him forward.
transformation.costlyChoice: After the sneeze wakes Fuzzby and Fuzzby warns him off, Keen tests the boundary with ‘Never … Ever?’ but then accepts this attempt is over and walks away without the honey.
transformation.exitBelief: I cannot make this honey mine just by wanting it and sneaking harder — at least not now.
transformation.exitAction: Keen leaves the honeycomb untouched and exits the attempt, while the nook returns to a calm that he has failed to conquer.

tapestry.physicalMotif: Approach-and-freeze: Keen’s body repeatedly reaches toward sweetness, then locks when the world answers back. The honeycomb stays still as the prize; Keen does all the visible negotiating around it.
tapestry.sonicMotif: Tiny betrayals of sound: CRUNCH, snore-bubble swell, POP, sneeze, then the soft return of ‘ZZZZZ …’ and Zenny’s ‘Ommmm…’. The scene’s comedy is the gap between Keen wanting silence and the nook refusing silence.
tapestry.colourAndLightProgression: Begin in warm golden morning temptation — dew sparkle and honey glow make the prize inviting. As pollen enters, the warmth becomes ticklish and unstable rather than purely cosy. End with the same morning calm restored, but now it feels smugly out of Keen’s reach.
tapestry.thematicVisualContrast: Busy wanting versus peaceful ownership: Keen is all knees, reaches, freezes and flinches; Fuzzby sleeps heavily on the honeycomb as if the boundary needs no effort; Zenny’s meditation is the quietest possible arrival after Keen’s noisy failure.
tapestry.openingClosingRhyme: Opening image: the honeycomb on the stump as a glowing prize Keen believes he can reach. Closing image: the honeycomb still on the stump, untouched, now reading as a boundary and a promise rather than an easy treat.

treatments.name: The Nook Tells on Him
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience feels like they are inside a living morning that cannot keep Keen’s secret. Every tiny sound becomes huge: dew, crunch, snore bubble, pollen, POP. Children giggle because Keen thinks he is sneaky while the whole place keeps announcing him. Adults read the familiar truth of a child trying to take a treat and being betrayed by his own little body and the room around him.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Keen owns the emotional drive: honey-pulled, self-consciously brave, and sure that trying harder equals being ready. But the camera does not fully obey him. It keeps letting the Buzzing Nook answer back, so the scene’s real opposition is not Fuzzby as a villain; it is the environment calmly refusing to become silent for Keen’s want.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: environmental participation. The ground crunches exactly when Keen needs quiet, Fuzzby’s sleep creates popping traps, pollen lands where Keen cannot resist it, and calm returns the moment Keen gives up. Secondary mechanism: escalating overcommitment — each freeze makes Keen’s next tiny reach more determined and more ridiculous.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Keen over-performs stealth: knees too high, paws held too carefully, eyes too wide, breath held too long, then a greedy lip lick that gives him away to us even if no one else sees. His freezes are not generic pauses; each one is a thought: ‘Still safe?’ then ‘Still want it.’ Fuzzby sleeps with total possession of the honeycomb; even asleep, he is the boundary. When he wakes, the warning comes from possessive drowsy certainty rather than meanness, then he falls back into sleep as if the matter is settled. Zenny’s late arrival is the opposite register: one calm, centered ‘Ommmm…’ that makes Keen’s whole mission look even busier in hindsight.
treatments.visualGrammar: Treat the Buzzing Nook as an accomplice with opinions. The frame keeps finding foreground grasses, dew beads, petals and pollen between Keen and the honey, so the prize is visible but never simply available. Morning gold begins as invitation, then becomes a spotlight exposing every mistake. The honeycomb remains the most stable object in the scene: Keen negotiates around it, the world tattles around it, and it never moves.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera travels with Keen’s temptation but repeatedly gets distracted by what will betray him. It may start near his high stepping feet, feel the crunch before it looks up, drift to a swelling snore bubble before Keen understands the danger, then return to him already frozen. The camera is not safe coverage; it is a nervous co-conspirator that keeps noticing evidence Keen wishes would disappear.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Keen supplies motion in bursts: approach, freeze, reach, recoil, recover, recommit. Fuzzby supplies heavy comic stillness, interrupted only by sleep mechanics and the brief possessive wake-up. Zenny’s stillness at the end is the final punctuation. The scene is built on busy wanting colliding with peaceful ownership.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth carries the joke: honeycomb and Fuzzby sit calm on the stump beyond layers of crunchy ground, drifting pollen and wildflowers. Keen is often separated from the prize by small natural obstacles that feel enormous at his scale of guilt. Pollen should cross depth before it reaches his nose, making the audience see the sneeze coming just before he does.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Begin with playful quiet and soft morning detail, then let each CRUNCH enlarge the suspense. Snore bubbles create a repeated breathing rhythm: grow, grow, POP, freeze. The second bubble should feel more dangerous because Keen chooses to keep going anyway. The pollen sequence breaks the pattern — instead of another freeze, his body finally cannot obey his plan. Fuzzby’s warning is a sleepy thunderclap, then the scene deflates into comic resignation and meditative calm.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by betrayal: a new sound, a swelling bubble, pollen entering the danger path, a changed emotion on Keen’s face, or comic punctuation after POP. Do not cut automatically from action to reaction. If Keen freezes and the world keeps moving around him, hold long enough for the audience to enjoy the gap between his still body and his racing thoughts. The final return to calm should not feel like a reset; it should feel like the nook has won this round.
treatments.openingImage: Golden dew sparkles around the honeycomb on the small stump, so inviting it seems to glow; behind layers of wildflowers, Keen’s exaggerated high-knee approach intrudes into the calm like a secret that is already too loud.
treatments.closingImage: The honeycomb remains untouched on the stump while Fuzzby slips back into ‘ZZZZZ …’; Keen has moved away from the prize, and Zenny’s calm ‘Ommmm…’ settles into the morning as if the nook has returned to its rightful rhythm.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not stage this as a clean side-on sneak toward a centered stump. That would make the environment wallpaper. The camera must let grasses, dew, pollen and bubble space interrupt the path, and it must sometimes discover the danger before Keen does. The challenge is readable geography without safe lanes: a four-year-old always knows honey, Keen and Fuzzby’s relationship in space, but the frame should feel alive enough to betray him.

treatments.name: The Sleeping Bee Is the Castle Gate
treatments.audienceExperience: The scene plays as a tiny suspense ritual around a sleeping guardian. Children lean in because the bee might wake at any second, and the POPs land like little jump-scares that are funny rather than frightening. Adults enjoy the precision of a child negotiating a boundary that is technically asleep but still very real.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The honeycomb-Fuzzby pairing governs the scene. Keen wants to enter that space, but the scene keeps insisting that the honey already belongs somewhere. Fuzzby is not active opposition at first; his sleep has authority. Keen’s emotional journey is measured by how close he dares to come to a boundary he knows he has not been invited past.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: anticipation to reversal. Each snore bubble promises one kind of danger — ‘will it wake him?’ — and the POP delivers Keen’s instant statue-freeze. The pollen later reverses Keen’s plan completely: the danger no longer comes from Fuzzby’s sleep but from Keen’s own nose. Secondary mechanism: concealment to revelation — Keen’s pretend control is revealed as helpless the moment the sneeze escapes.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Keen treats Fuzzby’s sleep like a formal challenge: every reach is slow, ceremonial and too careful, as if carefulness can become permission. His eyes stay locked on the honey until a sound forces them to Fuzzby; then his whole body snaps into innocence. Fuzzby’s sleeping ‘ZZZZZ …’ must feel weighty and possessive, not cute filler. His wake-up warning is half-dream, half-law: sleepy, grand, overlong, and absolutely convinced. After ‘…ever … ZZZZZ … never zzzz … bye keen,’ he has already emotionally closed the gate. Zenny does not judge aloud; her ‘Ommmm…’ arrives like the calm the scene was trying to have before Keen interrupted it.
treatments.visualGrammar: Make Fuzzby’s sleeping zone feel like a protected circle around the stump. The honeycomb is warm and close, but the air above it is occupied by snore bubbles that act like floating warning signs. The visual emphasis is on thresholds: Keen’s paw entering the protected air, a bubble swelling between him and the prize, pollen crossing into his face, then the boundary re-sealing when Fuzzby sleeps again.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like it is guarding the honey. It does not simply follow Keen; it often stays with the honeycomb and lets Keen’s paws, nose, or held breath enter the protected space. When the bubble grows, the camera’s attention belongs to the bubble, not to Keen, so the audience shares the terrible knowledge that a POP is coming. During the sneeze, the camera can be caught too close to the boundary, making the collapse feel bodily and immediate.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Fuzzby’s stillness is the scene’s authority. Keen moves around that stillness in tiny forbidden increments. The bubbles provide the only movement inside the protected zone until Keen invades it. When Fuzzby briefly wakes, his words create motion without needing chase or attack; then the return to sleep is a door closing. Zenny’s final stillness confirms that calm was always the natural state of this place.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use depth as a boundary map. Foreground: Keen’s cautious intrusions. Middle: bubble air and pollen drift. Background/core: honeycomb and sleeping Fuzzby on the stump. The scene should repeatedly show that Keen is not simply crossing distance; he is crossing permission. Pollen becomes the one environmental element that travels from the nook’s world into Keen’s body, defeating his careful exterior control.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm is lullaby versus alarm. Fuzzby’s ‘ZZZZZ …’ establishes soft sleep-time; bubble growth stretches the quiet; POP breaks it. Repeat the pattern once so children can anticipate and delight in it. Then replace POP with ACHOO, a bigger body-betrayal that wakes the boundary itself. Fuzzby’s long ‘never, ever, ever, ever, ever’ should feel comically too large for a half-awake warning, then collapse back into ‘ZZZZZ …’ before Keen can fully argue.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Prefer longer tension holds around bubbles and reaching paws; the laugh lives in waiting for the inevitable. Cuts should be paid for by threshold changes: paw closer, bubble larger, pollen entering, Fuzzby’s eye-line or wakefulness changing, Keen’s hope shrinking. Avoid cutting to every face by habit. Sometimes the funniest reaction is Keen frozen inside a frame still dominated by the thing he failed to take.
treatments.openingImage: Fuzzby asleep on top of the honeycomb like a tiny closed gate, ‘ZZZZZ …’ gently filling the golden morning while Keen’s high-kneed approach creeps toward the edge of that protected space.
treatments.closingImage: The gate has closed again: Fuzzby asleep on the honeycomb, the final sleepy fragments of ‘never zzzz … bye keen’ fading, while Zenny’s ‘Ommmm…’ places a calm seal over the untouched prize.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make Fuzzby passive background until his line. His sleeping body, bubbles and position on the honeycomb are the scene’s architecture. The challenge is to compose sleep as authority: the camera must sometimes privilege the stump and let Keen enter as the intruder. If we default to tracking the bear’s face the whole time, we lose the boundary story.

treatments.name: Keen’s Mighty Sneak Meets Tiny Reality
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience is invited into Keen’s self-image: he thinks this is a grand, brave, careful mission. The comedy comes when tiny reality keeps puncturing that private epic — CRUNCH, POP, pollen, ACHOO. Children laugh at the repeated collapse of his ‘sneaky’ pose. Adults recognise the sweet overconfidence of a child who has mistaken desire for readiness.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Keen’s imagination governs the emotional shape. The scene briefly lets his want feel enormous and heroic, then repeatedly reveals how small and exposed he actually is in the Buzzing Nook. His need is not taught; it is staged through the shrinking of his confidence. By the end, he is not crushed, just gently corrected by the world.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: status change. Keen starts each attempt as a self-appointed stealth expert, then every crunch, pop and sneeze reclassifies him as the loudest creature in the nook. Secondary mechanism: hiding failure — after each interruption, his freeze tries to pretend nothing happened, which is funnier than the sound itself.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Keen commits to the role in his head: lifted knees, careful paw placement, solemn concentration, then a lip lick that reveals the whole noble mission is really honey greed. His freezes should be too composed, as if he is performing ‘invisible’ for an audience. After the sneeze and Fuzzby’s warning, ‘Never … Ever?’ is not rebellion; it is a small child checking whether the boundary has any loophole left. Fuzzby, even sleepy, performs ownership with grand excess: his warning stretches far beyond the energy he has available, then runs out of steam into sleep. Zenny’s ‘Ommmm…’ is the scene’s final reality check: no fuss, no lecture, just calm continuing without Keen’s drama.
treatments.visualGrammar: Begin with Keen’s subjective grandeur and let the world cut him down to size. Low morning light and dew can make the honeycomb feel like a treasure from Keen’s perspective, but every interruption should widen the truth: he is in a small, bright, crunchy nook where nothing about him is invisible. The style moves from inflated mission-feel to plain comic fact.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera initially believes Keen just enough to make his confidence funny: it travels with his high knees and reaches as if the honey might truly be won. Then, at each betrayal, the camera abandons his self-importance for the incriminating detail — the crushed ground, the bubble, the pollen, Fuzzby’s sleepy authority, Zenny’s stillness. The camera is a gently teasing friend, not a neutral observer.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Keen’s movement is theatrical and over-controlled, which makes each involuntary reaction — flinch, freeze, sneeze — land harder. Fuzzby’s sleep is not just still; it is unbothered ownership. The honeycomb’s stillness becomes comic pressure: the prize does not chase him, tempt him verbally, or change; Keen generates all the fuss himself. Zenny’s final stillness turns his mission into a small ripple that has passed.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth should reveal the difference between Keen’s imagined mission and the real nook. At first, compress the world around honey and Keen’s desire so the prize feels close. As betrayals accumulate, open the space enough to show flowers, crunchy ground and drifting pollen as witnesses. By the end, Keen is spatially separated from the honeycomb in a way that makes his lost status visible.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Each cycle starts with renewed dignity and ends with involuntary exposure. First CRUNCH: his confidence dents. Second and third crunches: his performance becomes more careful and therefore funnier. First POP: he survives and recommits. Second POP: the audience knows he should stop, but he inches closer. Pollen and sneeze are the body’s final vote. Fuzzby’s ‘never, ever, ever, ever, ever’ stretches the defeat into comic ceremony; the last sleepy fragments let Keen’s hope leak away rather than explode.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts should puncture self-image. Stay with Keen when he is convincing himself he is capable; cut only when reality interrupts with new evidence or when his status changes. Do not assemble a routine sneak sequence. The edit should feel like a series of little truth-reveals: what Keen thinks he is doing, what the nook proves he is doing, then how he tries to recover his dignity.
treatments.openingImage: Keen’s high-knee tiptoe enters the golden morning with exaggerated seriousness, the honeycomb ahead reading in his eyes as a magnificent prize he is certain he can reach.
treatments.closingImage: Keen walks away without the honey, his mission reduced to a small retreat, while the honeycomb remains exactly where it was; Zenny’s calm ‘Ommmm…’ makes the untouched prize feel less like treasure and more like a lesson the nook is quietly saving for later.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not keep the whole scene at one cute low angle that flatters Keen’s adventure. We need the camera to change allegiance: briefly share his grandeur, then expose the tiny practical truth. The challenge is tonal elasticity without parody — make his mission feel real to him, funny to us, and always physically grounded in the morning nook.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: The Nook Tells on Him — strengthened by the sleeping-gate boundary and Keen’s punctured self-image
combinedFrom: The Sleeping Bee Is the Castle Gate

treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience feels like Keen’s giggling co-conspirator inside a living morning that keeps telling on him, until the untouched honey becomes a funny, gentle boundary rather than a prize he failed to win.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Select Treatment 1 as the spine. It best serves the scene truth: Keen is not naughty or opposed by a villain; he is a small bear whose wanting makes him overestimate his own stealth, while the nook calmly refuses to keep his secret. That gives us relationship, meaning, comedy and visual grammar in one engine. The honeycomb stays stable, Fuzzby’s sleeping ownership becomes the boundary, and Keen’s body supplies the escalating comedy. Fold in Treatment 2’s strongest idea: Fuzzby asleep on the honeycomb is not background but architecture — a protected zone Keen keeps entering without permission. Fold in Treatment 3’s best character lens: Keen briefly experiences the sneak as a mighty mission, and every CRUNCH, POP and sneeze gently shrinks that self-image back to child-sized reality. The combined approach gives the scene a strong energy curve: tempting calm, tiny suspense, repeated betrayal, body-collapse sneeze, sleepy warning, and restored calm with the honey still promising future story. It also gives the cinematography a dramatic job before beats exist: the camera is a nervous accomplice that keeps discovering the incriminating details Keen wishes would disappear.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: No selected element may depend on fixed screen lanes, keeping all characters visible, habitual action/reaction coverage, safe side-on staging, repeated close-up punctuation, mechanical shot counts, generic ‘cinematic’ language, or merely illustrating the script. Treatment 1 passes because it gives the environment agency and makes the camera participate in the dramatic question rather than cover it. Treatment 2 is not chosen alone because, if over-applied, the ‘castle gate’ idea could make the scene too static and shift emotional ownership away from Keen; we keep its boundary logic, not a rigid protected-circle diagram. Treatment 3 is not chosen alone because Keen’s ‘grand mission’ could become a flattering subjective routine or parody if it loses the nook’s active betrayal; we keep the status-puncture idea, not a generic sneaking-adventure frame. Any execution that stages a clean side-on sneak to a centered stump, cuts automatically from sound to face reaction, or keeps honey/Keen/Fuzzby constantly visible is rejected.

beats.sourceScript: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.whatChanges: The honeycomb changes from a simple glowing temptation into a guarded prize: Fuzzby’s sleeping ownership and the nook’s noisy floor make Keen’s private plan public to the audience.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives by recommitting after each betrayal; the Buzzing Nook counters by making every tiny movement audible or dangerous.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits for the next too-loud step or snore-bubble pop, enjoying that they see the trap Keen keeps trying to out-careful.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen high-knee tiptoes, freezes at each CRUNCH, spots the honeycomb, licks his lips, reaches anyway, then has to negotiate around Fuzzby asleep on top of the honey as the snore bubble grows and pops.
beats.consequence: Keen gets closer but not safer. The honey remains untouched, Fuzzby remains asleep, and the environment has established that silence will not cooperate.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The repeated freeze leaves Keen more determined and more ridiculous, handing the next beat a body already wound tight enough for pollen to defeat it.

emotionContract.entryState: Excited and self-consciously brave, treating the honey as something he can reach if he performs stealth carefully enough.
emotionContract.pressure: Every CRUNCH and the snore bubble threaten to wake Fuzzby, while the honey stays visible and tempting beyond small natural obstacles.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Keen chooses to keep reaching after each freeze instead of backing away, reading each survived sound as permission to continue.
emotionContract.exitState: Closer to the honey but tenser, with his confidence now dependent on his body staying perfectly controlled.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: High knees, paws held too carefully, eyes widening at the honey, lip lick, full-body freezes after each sound, and a reach that resumes despite Fuzzby sleeping on the honeycomb.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience knows the nook is louder and more alert than Keen wants to admit.

comedyContract.setup: Keen believes exaggerated care can make him silent enough to reach the honeycomb.
comedyContract.expectation: Each careful step should make him safer and closer to success.
comedyContract.disruption: The ground answers with CRUNCH, Fuzzby’s snore bubble grows into a popping trap, and the honey’s guardian remains physically on the prize even while asleep.
comedyContract.button: Fuzzby’s continued “ZZZZZ …” after the bubble business makes Keen’s huge effort look tiny against sleeping ownership.
comedyContract.hold: Hold on Keen frozen while the nook keeps softly moving around him, so the joke is his still body pretending his racing want has disappeared.

shots.physicalPerformance: Keen sneaks in already over-managed: knees lifted too high, paws held delicately, torso pitched toward the honey. Each noisy betrayal snaps him into a rigid full-body stop; desire restarts as a smaller, greedier reach. Fuzzby stays planted on the honeycomb, sleep-heavy, with snore bubbles turning his stillness into traps.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Keen is trying to make wanting look like skill: if he can perform stealth carefully enough, he can believe the honey is within reach. Fuzzby’s sleeping body makes ownership effortless.

phases.observableAction: Keen enters already mid-sneak, lifting his knees high, placing each foot with exaggerated care, and aiming his eyes and reaching paw toward the honeycomb.
The crunchy ground answers Keen’s careful steps, and snore bubbles near the honeycomb swell and burst in the same space he needs to cross.
Keen snaps into guilty full-body freezes after each betrayal, then restarts with a smaller, tighter reach toward the honey.
Fuzzby remains asleep on top of the honeycomb, covering the prize as bubble residue fades and the honey stays untouched.

characterTruths.substitutionTest: Zenny’s calm stillness would read as meditation, not sleeping ownership; Keen’s body would advertise wanting, not possession. Only Fuzzby can make the honey feel guarded through comic sleep.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Collapse Keen’s stealth mission, clarify Fuzzby’s honeycomb boundary, and leave the honey unresolved as a funny promise.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Anticipatory laughter, then comic relief when the sneeze destroys the plan.
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Gentle recognition that excitement and readiness are not the same thing, without shaming Keen.
storyIntent.outerAction: Pollen lands on Keen’s nose, he sneezes twice, Fuzzby wakes to warn him, Keen asks one loophole question, then walks away as Zenny meditates nearby.
storyIntent.innerAction: Keen moves from ‘I can still control this’ to ‘Maybe there is a loophole’ to ‘not this time.’
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Play the sneeze fight as heroic overcontrol applied to a silly body problem; play the retreat as lightly defeated, not crushed.
storyIntent.mutedRead: The drifting pollen, nose twitch, watery eyes, explosive recoil, Fuzzby eye-pop, guarded honey, Keen’s sagging sigh and Zenny’s settled pose tell the full story without dialogue.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The pollen finishes what crunchy ground and bubbles began; the nook refuses silence, then rewards surrender by becoming calm again.
storyIntent.soundStory: The scene peaks with “ACHOO!”, stumbles through the second “ACHOO!”, settles into Fuzzby’s sleep-mumbled boundary, then resolves into Zenny’s “Ommmm…” and ambient morning.
storyIntent.motifUse: Approach-and-freeze is broken by sneeze-and-retreat; the honeycomb’s stillness completes the opening/closing rhyme.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: The final hold is motivated by Keen’s thought changing from bargaining to acceptance; the scene does not cut away until the nook’s calm has visibly won.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Keen did not get the honey, Fuzzby owns and guards it even while sleepy, and Keen chooses to walk away.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: Whether Keen will try again later or how the honeycomb will matter next remains open.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Fuzzby’s eye-pop changes the sneeze from private body gag to public caught-in-the-act failure; Zenny’s stillness changes the failure into calm comic punctuation.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Keen is close enough to be caught but remains outside possession of the honey; by the end he has physically increased distance from the stump.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Fuzzby holds the boundary with almost no effort; Keen has desire but no leverage; Zenny’s calm has no force yet rebalances the scene.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: Keen still never touches the honeycomb; after the warning he avoids the prize by walking away.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: Keen’s eyes flick between honey, Fuzzby and the pollen threat; Fuzzby’s brief open-eyed attention lands on Keen as the trespasser; Zenny keeps eyes closed.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: Keen’s sneeze recoil and later drooped walk-away must read against the stable stump; Zenny’s cross-legged stillness must read as the opposite of Keen’s busy angles.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the beat before the first sneeze, the beat after Fuzzby’s eyes open, and the held calm after Zenny’s line.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Withhold score through the sneeze anticipation so breath, pollen and POP-like impact carry it; allow only a soft settling tone under the final calm if it does not compete with snoring and meditation.

shots.physicalPerformance: Keen fights the pollen with heroic over-control: nose twitching, eyes watering, body pulling inward until the sneeze snaps him backward. When caught, he tries a tiny polite recovery, is betrayed again, then shrinks into a hopeful check and a defeated walk away. Fuzzby wakes only enough to claim the space, then drops straight back to sleep. Zenny arrives as centered stillness.
shots.animationTiming: Protect the long inhale-fight-collapse before the first sneeze; the release should hit fast and jolt Keen’s balance without moving the honeycomb. Fuzzby’s eye-pop is sharp, his wakefulness brief and heavy. Keen’s final sigh and retreat slow the tempo before Zenny’s held calm button.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Keen is trying to hold his body together long enough to save the mission, then tries to save face once exposed. Fuzzby needs only sleepy certainty to hold the honey, and Zenny’s calm makes the whole scramble look small.

phases.observableAction: A yellow pollen puff drifts across the depth of the nook, reaches Keen’s face, and lands on his nose while the honeycomb remains just beyond him.
Keen’s nose twitches, his eyes water, his chest and mouth fight the breath, then his body snaps backward from the sneeze; he attempts a small polite recovery and is interrupted by a second sneeze.
Fuzzby’s eyes pop open on top of the honeycomb, he fixes on Keen long enough to deliver a drowsy possessive response, then his eyes close and his body settles back over the prize.
Zenny sits cross-legged on a leaf with eyes closed, barely moving except for one steady breath as the nook’s calm returns around the untouched honeycomb.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The pollen lands directly on Keen’s nose, triggering visible twitching, watery eyes, breath compression, and a sneeze strong enough to pull his reach back and upset his balance. The sound wakes Fuzzby, whose body remains on the honeycomb and blocks access without contact. After the exchange, Keen increases distance from the stump, leaving the honey still under Fuzzby’s body while Zenny’s still posture stabilizes the frame.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Keen changes from tight bodily control to exposed, wet-eyed recoil, then to a smaller drooped retreat. Fuzzby changes from asleep to briefly alert and back again, while Zenny introduces complete stillness after the commotion.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: The final image must clearly show that Keen has not touched or taken the honey, Fuzzby is asleep on top of it again, Keen has moved away from the prize, and Zenny’s calm presence has settled the nook.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Give the animator room to choose Keen’s exact pre-sneeze facial tremors, paw flutters, recoil shape, and final droop, provided the sneeze is visibly unavoidable and not harmful. Fuzzby’s wake-sleep switch may have small antenna, wing, or spectacle jiggle. Zenny may have minimal secondary leaf motion, but her body stays centered and quiet.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Supplied sequence lock: Keen is self-consciously brave and keeps trying to turn effort into proof that he is ready.
characterTruths.playableWant: He wants to keep the honey attempt alive first by controlling the sneeze, then by making the caught moment look harmless, then by checking for one last opening.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: His body betrays him before his plan can recover: nose twitch, watery eyes, breath clamp, recoil, awkward paw lift, and finally a lowered-shoulder walk away.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Over-controlled face before the release, sudden backward snap, embarrassed recovery posture, small hopeful lean toward Fuzzby, then a soft collapse into retreat.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Fuzzby would puff up and crash; Zenny would conserve motion. Only Keen makes a tiny body problem feel like a brave mission failing in public.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Fuzzby is the bigger warm comic bee whose physical comedy and possession are body-led, pompous-then-undercut, and never cruel.
characterTruths.playableWant: He wants the honeycomb to remain his without spending real energy on a fight.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He wakes abruptly, asserts ownership from the exact spot on the prize, then lets sleep reclaim him as if the matter is already settled.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Eye-pop impact, drowsy focus on Keen, body still anchored to the honeycomb, and an immediate drop back into heavy sleep.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen could not guard the prize while wanting it; Zenny’s dry calm would make the moment observational. Only Fuzzby can make a possessive response feel sleepy, comic, and warm instead of sharp.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Zenny is Fuzzby’s smaller, calm, dry counterweight: her stillness is the contrast that makes surrounding busyness funny.
characterTruths.playableWant: She wants to remain centered in the nook’s rhythm rather than join Keen’s scramble.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: She answers commotion by becoming more still: eyes closed, cross-legged balance, one even breath, no visible hurry.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Cross-legged leaf posture, closed eyes, minimal movement, and a calm held presence that contrasts with Keen’s recoil and retreat.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Fuzzby would fill the space with motion or sleepy possession; Keen would broadcast desire and embarrassment. Only Zenny can end the scene by making quiet stillness the punchline.

comedyStaging.staysVisible: Keep the honeycomb and Fuzzby’s sleeping claim visible through the sneeze payoff, so the audience never loses what Keen was risking everything to reach.
comedyStaging.contactAndWeight: Keen’s sneeze has enough force to snap his reach back and jolt his balance; nearby pollen and small flowers react lightly, while Fuzzby wakes from the sound rather than from being struck.
comedyStaging.payoffShape: The gag shape is inhale-fight-collapse: pollen approaches, Keen tries to contain it, “ACHOO!” bursts him out of stealth, recovery becomes a greeting, and the second “ACHOO!” ruins even that.
prohibitedStaging: Do not turn the sneeze into a blast that moves the honeycomb or harms Fuzzby.
Do not cut away before the audience sees Keen’s body lose the fight.
Do not make Fuzzby sharp or mean; the warning is sleepy possession, not cruelty.

voicePerformances.speaker: Fuzzby

voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: To make the honeycomb feel guarded without consciously addressing Keen.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen, indirectly; the honeycomb as claimed territory.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Oblivious comfort, fully planted in sleep.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Still asleep, but the snore has become a comic obstacle Keen must survive.

voicePerformances.rhythm: One rounded snore that grows lazily, then trails off into the ellipsis.

voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: sleep-thick, satisfied, totally unbothered by the chaos he is causing.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: To reassert the trap just as Keen thinks he can restart.
voicePerformances.subtext: Still mine. Still sleeping. Still impossible.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen, as the would-be honey thief being defeated by a nap.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Same heavy sleep, now funnier because Keen is trying again.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: A longer held danger that sets up Keen’s final bigger freeze.

voicePerformances.breaths: Low sleepy intake; loose exhale through the snore.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Snore bubble swells slowly while Keen’s greedy reach gets smaller and more careful.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The unchanging sleepy sound contrasts Keen’s elastic panic; Fuzzby’s stillness keeps winning without trying.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen: bright, impulsive, trying far too hard to be in control until his body betrays him.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: To hold the mission together and fail spectacularly in front of Fuzzby.
voicePerformances.subtext: Please, please do not notice me.

voicePerformances.breaths: A strained, rising inhale before the sneeze; no polite breath after, just stunned recovery.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen: eager and transparent; his politeness gets tiny when he knows he has been caught.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: To convince Fuzzby this is a normal, friendly visit and not a failed honey raid.

northStar.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is gently witnessed and welcomed.
northStar.childClearWant: Keen wants the honey without waking Fuzzby.

scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.purpose: Open on Keen’s honey-pulled stealth attempt and establish the Buzzing Nook as an active comic witness that refuses to keep his secret.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.dramaticQuestion: Can Keen reach the honeycomb without waking Fuzzby, or will the nook and his own body tell on him first?
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.entry: I can borrow enough boldness to sneak past Fuzzby and get the honey if I just keep going.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.exit: Keen leaves the honeycomb untouched and exits the attempt, while the nook returns to a calm that he has failed to conquer.

pointOfView: Keen’s tempted co-conspirator point of view, with the Buzzing Nook allowed to interrupt him as an opinionated witness.
Keen’s failed-control experience, countered by the nook’s calm authority and Fuzzby’s sleepy ownership.

dramaticBeats.beginning: The honeycomb changes from a simple glowing temptation into a guarded prize: Fuzzby’s sleeping ownership and the nook’s noisy floor make Keen’s private plan public to the audience.
dramaticBeats.development: Fuzzby wakes just enough to state the honeycomb boundary with drowsy possession. The honey changes from ‘almost mine’ to ‘definitely not now.’
dramaticBeats.turn: Keen asks “Never … Ever?”, hears Fuzzby fold the warning into sleep, then walks away as Zenny’s “Ommmm…” settles the space.
dramaticBeats.landing: Comic resignation replaces suspense: the scene lands on calm that is not a reset but the nook’s victory over Keen’s over-busy want.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Keen over-performs stealth with knees too high, paws too careful, eyes too wide and freezes that each read as a thought before his desire restarts him; Fuzzby’s sleep remains heavy and possessive.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Keen sneaks in already over-managed: knees lifted too high, paws held delicately, torso pitched toward the honey. Each noisy betrayal snaps him into a rigid full-body stop; desire restarts as a smaller, greedier reach. Fuzzby stays planted on the honeycomb, sleep-heavy, with snore bubbles turning his stillness into traps.

contract.playableIntention: Keen is trying to make wanting look like skill: if he can perform stealth carefully enough, he can believe the honey is within reach. Fuzzby’s sleeping body makes ownership effortless.

phases.observableAction: Keen enters already mid-sneak, lifting his knees high, placing each foot with exaggerated care, and aiming his eyes and reaching paw toward the honeycomb.

beats.sourceScript: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …

beats.whatChanges: The honeycomb changes from a simple glowing temptation into a guarded prize: Fuzzby’s sleeping ownership and the nook’s noisy floor make Keen’s private plan public to the audience.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives by recommitting after each betrayal; the Buzzing Nook counters by making every tiny movement audible or dangerous.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits for the next too-loud step or snore-bubble pop, enjoying that they see the trap Keen keeps trying to out-careful.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen high-knee tiptoes, freezes at each CRUNCH, spots the honeycomb, licks his lips, reaches anyway, then has to negotiate around Fuzzby asleep on top of the honey as the snore bubble grows and pops.
beats.consequence: Keen gets closer but not safer. The honey remains untouched, Fuzzby remains asleep, and the environment has established that silence will not cooperate.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The repeated freeze leaves Keen more determined and more ridiculous, handing the next beat a body already wound tight enough for pollen to defeat it.

shots.physicalPerformance: Keen sneaks in already over-managed: knees lifted too high, paws held delicately, torso pitched toward the honey. Fuzzby stays planted on the honeycomb, sleep-heavy, with snore bubbles turning his stillness into traps.

shots.physicalPerformance: Keen fights the pollen with heroic over-control: nose twitching, eyes watering, body pulling inward until the sneeze snaps him backward. When caught, he tries a tiny polite recovery, is betrayed again, then shrinks into a hopeful check and a defeated walk away. Fuzzby wakes only enough to claim the space, then drops straight back to sleep. Zenny arrives as centered stillness.
shots.animationTiming: Protect the long inhale-fight-collapse before the first sneeze; the release should hit fast and jolt Keen’s balance without moving the honeycomb. Fuzzby’s eye-pop is sharp, his wakefulness brief and heavy. Keen’s final sigh and retreat slow the tempo before Zenny’s held calm button.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Keen is trying to hold his body together long enough to save the mission, then tries to save face once exposed. Fuzzby needs only sleepy certainty to hold the honey, and Zenny’s calm makes the whole scramble look small.

phases.observableAction: A yellow pollen puff drifts across the depth of the nook, reaches Keen’s face, and lands on his nose while the honeycomb remains just beyond him.
Keen’s nose twitches, his eyes water, his chest and mouth fight the breath, then his body snaps backward from the sneeze; he attempts a small polite recovery and is interrupted by a second sneeze.
Fuzzby’s eyes pop open on top of the honeycomb, he fixes on Keen long enough to deliver a drowsy possessive response, then his eyes close and his body settles back over the prize.
Zenny sits cross-legged on a leaf with eyes closed, barely moving except for one steady breath as the nook’s calm returns around the untouched honeycomb.

After the exchange, Keen increases distance from the stump, leaving the honey still under Fuzzby’s body while Zenny’s still posture stabilizes the frame.

comedyStaging.contactAndWeight: Keen’s sneeze has enough force to snap his reach back and jolt his balance; nearby pollen and small flowers react lightly, while Fuzzby wakes from the sound rather than from being struck.
comedyStaging.payoffShape: The gag shape is inhale-fight-collapse: pollen approaches, Keen tries to contain it, “ACHOO!” bursts him out of stealth, recovery becomes a greeting, and the second “ACHOO!” ruins even that.
prohibitedStaging: Do not turn the sneeze into a blast that moves the honeycomb or harms Fuzzby.
Do not cut away before the audience sees Keen’s body lose the fight.

showrunnerJudgement: Pass. I tried to break this on the selected experience, but the scene still accumulates the right behaviour: Keen’s child-clear want is visible without explanation, the nook actively tattles on him, Fuzzby remains a sleepy boundary rather than an antagonist, and Zenny’s late stillness lands as a comic settling of the room. The honeycomb staying untouched is not just continuity; it becomes the gentle boundary and future promise the scene needs.
treatmentComparison: The storyboard preserves the treatment’s central pleasure: the audience is Keen’s giggling co-conspirator inside a morning that keeps betraying him. The camera is not merely covering a side-on sneak; it embeds behind dew and wildflowers, travels with Keen’s feet, then lets crunches, snore bubbles and pollen redirect attention. The honeycomb remains stable while Keen negotiates around it, which matches the signed argument of busy wanting versus peaceful ownership. The pollen beat correctly breaks the repeated crunch/bubble grammar by making Keen’s own body the final traitor. Fuzzby’s warning reads as possessive drowsy certainty, not meanness, and the closing return to Zenny’s “Ommmm…” restores calm as the nook’s victory rather than as a neutral reset. The main caution is density in S1.SH2: it must not rush the walk-away and Zenny button, because that final after-feeling is the scene’s proof that Keen has accepted this attempt is over.
packingJudgement: Packing passes. The split between S1.SH1 and S1.SH2 is protected by duration: the adjacent units combine to 53 seconds, so this is not an avoidable join under the 30-second policy. Both units are near-full and have clear jobs: S1.SH1 carries stealth setup, honey/Fuzzby reveal and repeated bubble escalation; S1.SH2 carries pollen collapse, boundary, loophole question, resignation and calm. S1.SH2 is dense, but it is still a coherent second arc rather than a needless fragmentation. The provider audit is acceptable, with the note that the final Zenny calm must be protected in timing and not swallowed by the dialogue-heavy warning exchange.
